passages.text: The difficulty, my friends, is not to avoid death, but to avoid unrighteousness; for that runs faster than death.

If you think that by killing men you can prevent some one from censuring your evil lives, you are mistaken; that is not a way of escape which is either possible or honourable; the easiest and the noblest way is not to be disabling others, but to be improving yourselves.
passages.note: facing criticism by self-improvement, not silencing critics

passages.text: Now if you suppose that there is no consciousness, but a sleep like the sleep of him who is undisturbed even by dreams, death will be an unspeakable gain. For if a person were to select the night in which his sleep was undisturbed even by dreams, and were to compare with this the other days and nights of his life, and then were to tell us how many days and nights he had passed in the course of his life better and more pleasantly than this one, I think that any man, I will not say a private man, but even the great king will not find many such days or nights, when compared with the others. Now if death be of such a nature, I say that to die is gain; for eternity is then only a single night.
passages.note: fear of death; death as peaceful sleep

passages.text: Wherefore, O judges, be of good cheer about death, and know of a certainty, that no evil can happen to a good man, either in life or after death.
passages.note: comfort facing death; goodness cannot be harmed

passages.text: The hour of departure has arrived, and we go our ways--I to die, and you to live. Which is better God only knows.
passages.note: parting, mortality, humility about what is better
